chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man marries a woman during her waiting period and consummates the marriage with her, she becomes permanently forbidden to him, whether he was aware or ignorant. And if he did not consummate with her, she becomes permissible for the ignorant one, but not for the other (the aware one).

key_terms.عَالِمًا كَانَ أَوْ جَاهِلًا: whether he was aware or ignorant
key_terms.لَمْ تَحِلَّ لَهُ أَبَدًا: she became permanently forbidden to him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries a woman during her waiting period and then divorces her before consummation?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify the permanence of the marital bond when a man marries a woman during her 'iddah. The hadith establishes that consummation renders the marriage irrevocable for all, while non-consummation allows for a distinction based on the man's knowledge, reflecting the Shia emphasis on intent and awareness in legal validity.
